Arrive at La Aurora International Airport. Your driver meets you at the airport for the transfer to Antigua. The drive is about 40 km and takes approximately one hour.

Overnight at Porta Antigua in a Standard double room, with breakfast included.

Guatemala City: a long stone façade with towers and arched windows
Antigua – Lake Atitlán – San Juan La Laguna – Santiago Atitlán

Your driver takes you to Panajachel on the shores of Lake Atitlán. On the final descent from Sololá to Panajachel, the view opens up across the lake and the surrounding volcanoes.

The day takes you to Tz’utujil Maya communities, starting in San Juan, one of the cleanest and best-kept towns around the lake. It has art galleries, and many local painters work in naïve and primitivist styles. The town is also home to women’s cooperatives. You can see handweaving and natural fabric dyeing and meet local midwives, known as comadronas, who grow medicinal herbs and use them in natural remedies.

Traditional farming, fishing, reed-mat weaving and textile making remain part of daily life. We stop at a local café to try Guatemalan coffee.

We then cross the lake by boat to Santiago Atitlán. The town was founded in 1547 at the foot of the Tolimán Volcano. It has around 32,000 residents, 95% of whom are Tz’utujil Maya. Local residents fish, farm and make traditional canoes known as cayucos.

We visit the Catholic church, where Catholic and Maya religious traditions intertwine, pass the town hall and return to Panajachel.

Overnight at Hotel Atitlan. Meals: breakfast.
